subject: OrchidPay inference errors and high latency — VPC peering impact
messages:
From: Ravi Desai <ravi@orchidpay.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: OrchidPay inference errors and high latency

Hi Nikhil,

We started seeing a big regression against Redwood for our payment-inference endpoint around 07:40 UTC. Symptoms: a spike in 5xxs (~12% over last 20m), median latency up from ~110ms to ~900ms, and request throttling from our side due to long tail. The issue is affecting checkout traffic — traffic dropped ~35% when retries exhausted.

Attached are two things: a short trace capture (orchidpay_trace_20270815.txt) and a CSV with sample request IDs and timestamps. We also opened a ticket with our cloud partner (CloudPortal) who mentioned they saw NAT session exhaustion and some DNS SERVFAILs originating from our VPC around the same time.

Can you confirm whether this looks like anything on Redwood's side (peering/egress/DNS)? Our SREs are standing by and can share traceroutes if helpful.

Ravi Desai

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-08-15 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: OrchidPay inference errors and high latency — initial findings

Team — quick summary of what SRE sees after correlating logs and traces:

- Spike in DNS SERVFAILs and increased DNS latency for queries originating from OrchidPay VPC blocks that are peered to our us-west-2 edge (seen 07:36–07:55 UTC).
- Packet captures show UDP DNS fragments and some truncated responses when traffic traverses a specific CloudPortal proxy (same hop Elena called out). Devices on that proxy are dropping fragments leading to retries and long tails.
- Additionally, we observe elevated TCP retransmits and a small percentage of 5xxs correlated to requests that experienced DNS resolution failures then retried multiple times.

Immediate mitigations we've enacted:
- Failover: Temporarily routed OrchidPay traffic away from the affected peering to our us-east-1 endpoint (transparent to the app) — this dropped the error-rate by ~70% in our test window.
- DNS fallback: Configured a resolver fallback for OrchidPay (10.200.4.5) to avoid UDP truncation over the proxy; TTL lowered for faster switchover.
- Engaged CloudPortal NOC to request: (a) inspect/patch proxy that drops UDP fragments, (b) validate NAT pool sizing and conntrack limits.

Next steps:
- CloudPortal to confirm root cause and ETA to remediate proxy behavior.
- We'll run a 2-hour observation window and then discuss a permanent fix (peering rehome, DNS configuration, or transit change).
- If OrchidPay wants a dedicated route (Reserved/Dedicated) while they validate, we can give numbers and a temporary credit.

Monica Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Redwood: short-term action and exec update for OrchidPay

Ravi / Elena — I'm sorry for the disruption. Quick note on our plan and compensation:

What we did (completed):
- Rerouted your traffic off the affected peering into our us-east-1 endpoint (transparent) — this is live and we see errors falling back to normal.
- Enabled DNS fallback and lowered TTL for faster recovery if CloudPortal retries.

What we will do (next 24h):
- Work with CloudPortal to remove UDP fragment drops or move peering to a path that does not go through the proxy.
- Provide a postmortem within 48 hours.
- Offer a service credit for the affected window; I'll coordinate details with your procurement team if you want.

If you prefer not to rely on peering while they remediate, we can fast-track a Dedicated route for the affected prefixes — Monica will share cost/time estimates.

Again, apologies. We'll keep the incident channel updated every hour for the next 4 hours.
